text: Primary-source runtime shortlist, not selection or download: (1) amrlib offers MIT code, macOS-capable CPU inference, and separately downloaded sentence-to-graph models including a 492 MB BART-base model (reported AMR3 Smatch 82.3); first use also downloads base-model/tokenizer assets, so code, checkpoint, base-model, training-data lineage, and hashes all need admission. (2) IBM transition-amr-parser offers Apache-2.0 code, official AMR3 structured-BART checkpoints and word-node alignments; its documented macOS path uses CPU torch-scatter and legacy Python/PyTorch-era dependencies, so compatibility risk is higher. (3) SPRING is CC BY-NC-SA and pinned to old transformers/torch, so it is not a default candidate. No option is authorized. Official sources: github.com/bjascob/amrlib, github.com/bjascob/amrlib-models, amrlib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/install/, github.com/IBM/transition-amr-parser, github.com/SapienzaNLP/spring.
